title: PPE supports safe work
completeCaptionText:
Personal Protective Equipment, or PPE, is equipment worn to reduce exposure to a hazard. It supports a safe method; it does not make an unsafe site or unauthorized task acceptable. The right combination depends on the job, the material and the conditions.

Sturdy work boots provide grip and foot protection. Where impact or crushing hazards exist, the trainer specifies suitable protective toe caps, such as steel-toed boots. Long sleeves and trousers can reduce scratches, sun exposure and insect contact; a wide-brimmed hat helps against the sun. Clothing must also suit heat and the work being done.

Use eye protection selected for the hazard. Safety glasses used for particles are not automatically a substitute for chemical splash goggles. Gloves suitable for general soil work protect hands and can reduce sample contamination, but they are not necessarily suitable for a chemical.
